label: input z at original positions 3-5
explanation: Fires only when the input token is z during the original (pre-DEL) phase at positions 3, 4 or 5 (rate ~100% there). It also fires weakly on about 18% of z inputs at position 2, and never on z at positions 0-1 or 6+. It never fires on any other token, or in the delimiter or copy phase (even when z is fed back). Magnitude is highest at positions 3-4 (top examples are z at t=4) and lower at t=5, with t=2 activations weakest. A repeated z (in_first=0) has a lower rate. Sequence length and earlier tokens have little effect.

issues: Minor inaccuracy: the explanation says 'a repeated z (in_first=0) fires at a lower rate', but at t=3-5 a repeated z fires every time (test precision 1.0 on 5075 steps for in_first==0 & t in 3..5). The lower rate only shows up at t=2: about 1.4% for a repeated z (1178 predicted steps) against about 19% for a first z. That part of the explanation should be limited to t=2.

The misses are not a systematic class. On the test split all 3029 missed activations are weak z inputs at t=2 (activations about 0.03-0.10 of max), together only 0.7% of activation mass. There are 0 false positives.

Other claims check out. The feature is silent in the delimiter phase. In the copy phase it fired once out of about 2.7M steps (dev), and on the test split z fed back as input in the copy phase has precision about 1e-5. It is zero at t=0-1 and at t>=6, and it never fires on tokens other than z. Each firing is weaker at t=5 than at t=3: t=5 has 0.149 of the mass over 10954 steps, t=3 has 0.438 over 16559. The by-L variation is explained by which positions exist in a sequence of that length.
